overview.text: Today's developments span long-sequence modeling, video reasoning, world models, and new hardware architectures. Stable Gated DeltaNet-2 addresses recurrent state instability to improve efficient linear attention for long sequences. In vision and video, coding agents are emerging as stronger visual reasoners than video models, while ShowNow introduces fine-grained speculative streaming to resolve input latency in interactive world models. Additionally, time-series foundation models face new evaluation frameworks through zero-shot forecasting leaderboards. In hardware and infrastructure, Trainium3 inference and microarchitecture is analyzed for performance and TCO, alongside applications like generating videos with LTX-2.5. Generalist computer-using agents are also being benchmarked on long-horizon workflows across platforms, and multimodal safety research explores learning to intervene rather than relying on blanket refusals when visual context alters safety boundaries.

entries.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
entries.summary: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states.
entries.why: This work directly targets recurrent state instability to improve efficient linear attention for long-sequence modeling tasks.

entries.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
entries.summary: A foundation model for time series is pretrained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets.
entries.why: This establishes resolution reporting to properly evaluate zero-shot time-series foundation models on held-out datasets.

entries.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
entries.summary: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out?
entries.why: Coding agents are demonstrated to be stronger visual reasoners than native video generation models.

entries.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
entries.summary: Interactive world models must generate video continuously while responding promptly to user actions. Real-time throughput alone leaves input latency unresolved: coarse generation blocks delay action updates, and generation after input adds work to the response path.
entries.why: This approach addresses input latency in interactive world models using fine-grained speculative streaming for responsive generation.

entries.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
entries.summary: Computer-using agents are increasingly expected to complete realistic user goals rather than isolated GUI actions.
entries.why: This benchmarks generalist computer-using agents on realistic long-horizon workflows across multiple platforms.

entries.title: Generation as Reverse Encoding
entries.summary: Pretrained visual representations accelerate generative learning by abstracting away appearance and spatial detail. Yet the same abstraction makes the return to pixels far harder, shifting much of the burden onto a larger decoder.
entries.why: This examines how pretrained visual representations shift the generative learning burden onto larger decoders.

entries.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
entries.summary: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved.
entries.why: This investigates selective interventions for multimodal safety instead of standard blanket refusals.

entries.summary: Better Perf TCO vs NVIDIA GB300, First Principles Physics-Based Architecture, High MFU and MBU, UBenchX, Low Latency, Alisa Liu vs Eileen Gu
entries.why: This analysis details Trainium3 inference performance, microarchitecture, and TCO compared to NVIDIA infrastructure.

entries.title: Astra 6.2’s Brain Gets Smart But Its Head Gets Dumb
entries.why: This analysis discusses the trade-offs in intelligence and behavior found in Astra 6.2.

entries.title: I don’t expect superposition in transformer MLP neurons
entries.summary: I currently believe that in a typical (well trained and under-parametrized) transformer model, there is something like superposition-type compression in the residual stream, but not in the MLP neurons.
entries.why: This alignment discussion examines the presence of superposition in transformer residual streams versus MLP neurons.
